elements.element: Licensee may terminate the Agreement for convenience during the committed Initial Period.
elements.evidence: The added language gives Licensee an unqualified right to terminate the Agreement for convenience, which applies during the 36-month Initial Period.

elements.element: Licensee may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on thirty (30) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires thirty (30) days' prior notice.

elements.element: Licensee's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires prior written notice to Licensor.

elements.element: Upon Licensee's termination for convenience, Licensor must refund prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Licensor to refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

elements.element: The refund of prepaid fees must be calculated on a pro-rata basis through the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: Although the words 'pro rata' are not used, refunding prepaid fees attributable to the period after the effective date operationally provides the required time-based pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Licensor must have no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: No termination-for-convenience right is granted to Licensor. Licensor's existing immediate termination right is expressly triggered by Licensee breach and therefore is not a convenience right.

elements.element: Licensee may terminate the Agreement for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added language gives Licensee an unqualified termination-for-convenience right applicable during the Initial Period.

elements.element: Licensee's termination-for-convenience notice period must be between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: The clause specifies thirty (30) days' prior written notice rather than a notice period within the 60–90 day fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee imposed on Licensee must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no early-termination fee, so the condition requiring compliance with the three-month cap is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If Licensor has a termination-for-convenience right, it may exercise that right only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Licensor is not granted any termination-for-convenience right. Its breach-based termination right is not a convenience right, so the condition is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If Licensor has a termination-for-convenience right, Licensor must provide ninety (90) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Licensor is not granted any termination-for-convenience right, so the condition requiring a 90-day notice restriction is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The operative language fully reaches the preferred position: Licensee receives a 30-day written-notice convenience right and a functionally pro-rata refund, while Licensor receives no convenience right during the committed term. The fallback is independently not satisfied because its specified 60–90 day customer notice period is absent. The redline is not minimal because it unnecessarily adds a partial-termination right ('in whole or in part') and makes an unrelated correction to the extension provision. It otherwise preserves the agreement's unrelated commercial terms and introduces no contradiction, though the partial-termination language lacks mechanics identifying what may be terminated and how the corresponding refund is allocated.
